invalid_because: the free and flat arms are optima on different meshes, so their difference is a discretisation mismatch and not a measurement of the extra axis; the gain is flat in the nuisance grid, which is the signature of that
note: The size constraint of the Proposition runs over a continuum; a program can impose it only at finitely many nuisance values, and a rule reading the extra coordinate can sit in the gaps.  So a positive gain at any finite grid is expected, and the question is whether it goes to zero as the grid fills in.  The flat arm is solved on the two-dimensional mesh, since a rule constant across the extra axis is a function of (T, lambda_hat); that is exact and it removes the equality rows whose size made the first attempt fail.
